item.title: a small guide to forms
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
A quick write-up on forms, mostly so future me stops relearning it.

why it matters

Forms shows up across web work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Prefer the obvious solution; clever costs interest forever.
  • The fix that survives is the one the next person can understand.
  • Write it down once, link to it everywhere.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: the case for forms
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
Short post: forms is one of those things that looks simple until it isn’t.

why it matters

Forms shows up across web work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Measure before you change anything; intuition is a poor profiler.
  • Start with the smallest thing that works, then make it boring on purpose.
  • Most of the value is in deleting, not adding.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: what i learned about forms
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
Every few months forms bites me again. This is what finally stuck.

why it matters

Forms shows up across web work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Name it after what it does, not after how it does it.
  • Prefer the obvious solution; clever costs interest forever.
  • If it is hard to test, that is the design telling you something.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.
